title: Test did you mean prototype against E064 mutation set
hypothesis: The E067 did you mean prototype will correctly identify a high proportion of E064 false accepts as did you mean cases, with recall >= 0.80 and specificity >= 0.90

kill_gate.assessment: Hypothesis falsified. Neither approach achieves both thresholds.

raw_evidence.mutation_names_file: EXPERIMENTS/064-remedy-existence/raw/mutations.json (613 entries with arm/ecosystem/intended/seed; the 576 this experiment scored are a subset. A local mutation-names.txt copy was removed on 2026-10-09: it was byte-redundant with this committed source and its 576 lines tripped the doc-lint cap.)

conclusion: HYPOTHESIS FALSIFIED. The E067 did you mean prototype correctly identifies 0% of E064 false accepts (recall = 0.0). The edit-distance baseline achieves 100% recall but 0% specificity (flags all names as similar). The problem is fundamentally semantic: near-miss package names that resolve to different projects cannot be distinguished from syntactically similar names that resolve to the intended project using deterministic suffix/prefix or edit-distance methods alone. This closes the loop on E064's untested observation about "did you mean" warnings.

LANDING_NOTE.note: No protocol was written before this run; the predeclared thresholds are the two in kill_gate. Verdict unchanged by E071 - this experiment never read a view_count field. See README.md for the protocol-after-the-fact reading and its ceiling.
